episodes.203911: Scattered thunderstorms produced localized flooding during the afternoon hours.
episodes.203927: During the late afternoon and early evening of the 4th, slow moving thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall and flooding to portions of west-central and southwest central Indiana.  Flooding was most significant in southeastern Vigo County near Blackhawk where a video showed flash flooding of a field and nearby road.  Later in the day, flash flooding also occurred in Daviess County and Lawrence County with two major roads flooded.  Total rainfall estimates were as high as 3-5 inches in these areas.
episodes.203967: Anomalously high deep layer moisture over the area with strong moisture transport. Isentropic lift and favorable divergence aloft in the right entrance region of an upper level jet streak supported widespread rain which was moderate to heavy at times. This led to isolated flash flooding.
episodes.204119: A supercell severe thunderstorm tracked south from eastern Morgan county to  Washington County and then into Lincoln County. The storm produced very large hail across Lincoln County, up to three inch diameter hail.
episodes.204309: Enough instability and moisture was present in the local atmosphere to generate a few severe thunderstorms.
episodes.205168: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in a summertime airmass with a couple of severe storms occurring in Lowndes county with impacts to trees and power lines.  In addition, a very moist airmass and weak steering flow led to flash flooding across portions of southwest Georgia.
episodes.205215: A weak trough to the west, moving into the Tennessee and Ohio Valley regions, brought several upper-level disturbances across western portions of central North Carolina. Within a broad area of very anomalous moisture, several instances of flash flooding were reported across Stanly County during the afternoon hours.
episodes.205359: A cluster of southward moving storms across eastern Colorado led to wind gusts of 60-63 mph in Kit Carson and Cheyenne counties, along with penny sized hail in Kit Carson county.
episodes.205362: A cluster of showers and storms moved out of eastern Colorado into northwest Kansas leading to wind gusts up to 70 mph and a plume of dust near Edson, KS.
episodes.205377: Several severe storms moved across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska, dropping large hail and producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.206019: Thunderstorms developed over parts of western and central North Dakota in an area of elevated instability as an upper level short-wave trough approached. One storm produced 60 mph wind gusts to the southeast of Mercer in Sheridan County during the mid-afternoon. Elevated low level moisture was noted over south-central North Dakota where thunderstorms formed in the late afternoon and early evening. Some of these storms produced very heavy rain over McIntosh County, mainly to the east and northeast of Ashley. Over three inches of rain fell during a short period of time to result in flash flooding with water filling low lying areas and overflowing some rural roads.
episodes.206293: Southwesterly flow aloft continued across the Northern Rockies into August 4. An embedded wave within the troughing was favorably timed in the afternoon hours to result in scattered showers and thunderstorms. Flow aloft increased with this wave, which allowed for gusty winds to be translated to the surface. Only one instance of severe caliber winds were observed on this day.
episodes.206577: A line of storms produced large hail and high winds during the afternoon and evening of August 5th, and into the early morning hours of August 6th. The largest sized hail measured at 3 inches in diameter was observed in Hoven. Later in the evening, a peak wind gust of 99 mph was recorded on a weather station out at Sandy Shore State Park, while the Watertown Regional Airport ASOS would record a peak gust of 68 mph. Over 40 trees were topped or downed as a result of these winds around the Lake Kampeska area. Additional sporadic tree and crop damage was noted elsewhere across northeast South Dakota. ||Heavy rainfall would also lead to flooding with reports of several roads overtopped by water in the city of Watertown, the towns of Britton, Agency Village, and Wilmot, as well as portions of rural Codington, Roberts, and Marshall counties. Already saturated soils from a wet spring and summer were unable to absorb the 2 to 4 inches of rainfall, with the COOP observer in Wilmot measuring 3.63 inches and 3.31 inches of rainfall from a CoCoRaHS observer 1 mile south southeast of Kidder. These heavy rains would result in river flooding, mainly across the Big Sioux and its tributaries.
episodes.206665: A shortwave trough and closed low reached the Quad State from the northwest during the morning of the 4th. The arrival of the shortwave preceded peak heating by several hours, limiting convective potential. Shear was very weak and instability limited. Slow-moving storms did produce torrential rainfall, with significant flooding issues reported in the Midtown area of Paducah before sunset.
episodes.206667: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms developed on the 5th over Southern Illinois as a shortwave trough was positioned over the area. MLCAPE values were over 1000J/kg, while shear was limited. A funnel cloud was reported north of Fairfield.
episodes.206782: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coast.
episodes.206785: A thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust in Orlando.
episodes.206786: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along and offshore from the coast.
episodes.206894: A surface front and mid-level energy encountering a moderately unstable and deep moisture environment led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds and heavy rainfall across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.206896: A surface front and mid-level energy encountering a moderately unstable and deep moisture environment led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds and heavy rainfall across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.206899: A surface front and mid-level energy encountering a moderately unstable and deep moisture environment led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds across coastal waters.
episodes.207058: Storms developed along the Black Hills just to the west and south of Sturgis during the rally. A storm coming off the Black Hills was able to produce a funnel cloud on the west side of Rapid City that had a lot of exposure.
episodes.207098: A isolated supercell developed within northwest flow over the region and trekked southward across Bent and Las Animas Counties, dropping significant hail during its lifespan.
episodes.207099: An isolated severe thunderstorm pushed eastward across far southern Baca County, producing large hail.
episodes.207151: A waterspout occurred southeast of Puerto Rico along a Vieques and St. Thomas streamer steered by northeasterly winds.
episodes.207156: A hot and unstable airmass was in place on the evening of August 5th.  A strong cap kept convection at a minimum, but one strong storm developed across Sullivan County and moved south before weakening.  The storm had damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.207196: A large area of showers and thunderstorms originating across south Florida produced an outflow boundary, which moved southwest of Cape Sable and acted as a focus for additional thunderstorm development.  Gale force wind gusts occurred north of Big Pine Key.
episodes.207224: Slow-moving thunderstorms impacted areas north of Ishpeming during the afternoon of the 5th, producing one report of large hail and rainfall of 3���5 inches in 3 hours. No significant flooding was reported.
episodes.207266: An area of heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina Piedmont in association with a surface low and stalled frontal boundary draped over the Coastal Plain. Localized very heavy rainfall resulted in urban and small stream flash flooding in south Charlotte.
episodes.207301: An isolated thunderstorm produced wind gusts up to 61 mph across northern Rosebud County.
episodes.207302: A thunderstorm occurred over Powder River County, producing heavy rain amounts nearing 3 inches and hail up to 1.25 inches.
episodes.207337: An area of heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms developed over the South Carolina Piedmont in association with a surface low and stalled frontal boundary draped over the Coastal Plain. Localized very heavy rainfall resulted in flash flooding across portions of central and southern York County.

Trained spotter reported a stalled vehicle due to ponding of water on Dogwood Avenue near the intersection of  Peach Street. Additional areas of poor drainage led to standing water in portions of downtown Ridgeway.

Emergency manager and stream gauges reported flash flooding developed in south Charlotte, mainly along Little Sugar Creek and Little Hope Creek after 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in just a couple of hours. Little Hope Creek overflowed its banks and inundated part of Mockingbird Lane. Little Sugar Creek flooded a portion of Wakefield Dr, covered a part of Reece Rd with a couple of feet of water, and approached some homes south of Archdale Dr. Emergency manager reported multiple swift water rescues of motorists in south Charlotte. Media reported multiple cars stranded in floodwater in the Pineville area.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed across central and southern York County after 3.5 to 5.5 inches of rain fell in just a few hours. Inundation of Wilson Chapel Rd occurred in the Sharon area, likely due to Bullock Creek overflowing its banks. One lane of Bookout Rd in McConnells was flooded by water from South Fork Fishing Creek. A tributary of Stony Fork flooded Stallcup Rd just southwest of Rock Hill. Phil Grant Rd was washed out near Strait Rd near the Chester County line due to a small drainage. Additionally, extensive yard flooding was reported in a neighborhood on the north side of Rock Hill due to Big Dutchman Creek overflowing its banks. However, other than water entering a couple of outbuildings, no structures or roads were impacted in this area.
